article_title: Rewarding How Models Think Pedagogically: Integrating Pedagogical Reasoning and Thinking Rewards for LLMs in Education
citation: Unggi Lee, Jiyeong Bae, Jaehyeon Park, Haeun Park, Taejun Park, Younghoon Jeon, Sungmin Cho, Junbo Koh, Yeil Jeong, Gyeonggeon Lee. (2026). Rewarding How Models Think Pedagogically: Integrating Pedagogical Reasoning and Thinking Rewards for LLMs in Education. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14560
title: 82-code educational codebook for analyzing LLM tutor behavior
description: An 82-code educational codebook developed through grounded theory methodology by two educational technology experts and two mathematics education experts, used to label over 150,000 tutor-response sentences across experimental conditions with GPT-5-mini. The article states the codebook comprises "82 codes organized into four major categories": Mathematical Problem Solving, Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching, Cognition and Metacognition, and Pedagogical Intent Utterances. It enables systematic, statistically validated comparison of tutoring behavior across training conditions.
requirements: Expert coder consensus through open, axial, and theoretical-integration coding phases; LLM-based automatic labeling of sentence-level data
constraints: Relies on LLM-based labeling which the authors note may introduce systematic biases
target_learners: Researchers and designers of LLM tutoring systems
target_learning_goals: Systematic analysis of tutor pedagogical behavior across cognitive, metacognitive, and pedagogical dimensions
examples: Applied to label over 150,000 sentences across the five experimental conditions, revealing significant differences in mathematical problem-solving content and praise rates
